subject: showerhead biofilms and mycobacteria
title: What If You Never Cleaned Your Shower Head?

scenes.text: What if you never cleaned your shower head? Scrubbing it might not even help.
scenes.keywords: shower head water spray close up

scenes.text: Every shower feeds a thin slime inside the nozzle called a biofilm, packed with bacteria that cling to the walls.
When scientists tested about fifty shower heads from nine US cities, roughly one in three held a lung-disease bacterium.
Inside some of them, these germs reached over a hundred times the levels found in the tap water itself.
Then the twist: one shower head cleaned with bleach had three times more of them when tested months later.
These bacteria shrug off chlorine. The good news: most are harmless, and researchers say there's no reason to fear showering.

description:
What if you never cleaned your shower head? A 2009 University of Colorado study of about 50 showerheads from nine US cities found roughly 30% carried significant levels of Mycobacterium avium, some at more than 100 times the levels in the water supply, and one bleach-cleaned showerhead showed a threefold rise months later.
A 2018 follow-up of 656 households found mycobacteria were the most common bacteria in showerhead slime; most are harmless, and the researchers say there is no reason to fear showering.
